scope: Independent whole-object semantic and item-identity review of the exact frozen v1 proposal; not whole-N07 cross-unit, producer, source, consumer, admission, native, Premium, or full-BIZQ acceptance.

authorNotesSnapshot.role: author hypothesis only; not acceptance evidence

findings.finding: These predecessor/current pairs change the primary decision rather than merely adding decisive protocol facts to the same answer: the old visible cases concern domain transaction rules (for example, settled payout idempotency or room cancellation consistency), while the current items ask separate wire-format, presence, field-identity, representation, or signing decisions. The old accepted option is one generic owner/defaulting rule applied to those domain facts; the new keys are specific operations with different meanings. Same unit label alone does not establish same question identity.
findings.requiredCorrection: Use each corresponding reserved question ID for the changed primary decision/archetype; keep only items i012 and i015 on their current question IDs, where the visible predecessor and current objectives both concern reproducible immutable result provenance and traceable corrected-invoice history. Existing current accepted option IDs are appropriately new and must remain bound to their meanings. This is a meaning-based disposition, not a replacement quota.

findings.finding: The keyed option is uniquely longest by raw character count in 14 of 18 items (i001, i002, i003, i005, i006, i007, i009, i010, i011, i013, i014, i015, i017, i018). The actual distractors are often individually relevant, but the repeated form gives a test-taking shortcut independent of the protocol facts, especially where the key combines multiple clauses and the competing choices are short fragments.
findings.requiredCorrection: Revise only the options whose actual comparison gives a reliable length cue: preserve the correct decision while making the nearest competing policy complete and case-specific, or make the key concise without omitting a necessary condition. Re-run existing option-ID scoring/feedback checks if option meanings change. No equal-word-count, minimum-option-count, or zero-warning rule is imposed.

findings.finding: The stem says archived meter messages contain field number 6 named legacy_peak and that future code must not reinterpret those bytes. That supports reserving field number 6 for binary wire compatibility, but it does not say that archived ProtoJSON or TextFormat payloads containing the field name are retained. The keyed answer and explanation require reserving both number and name; name reservation is specifically relevant to those textual representations.
findings.requiredCorrection: State that retained/replayed ProtoJSON or TextFormat payloads use the old name, or narrow the keyed decision to the visible binary-tag requirement. Keep the discriminator tied to the existing schema-retirement objective.

cohortAssessment: The new set has meaningful, distinct serialization decisions across field addition/defaults, presence, retirement, JSON naming, enums, format dispatch, unknown-field forwarding, collection shape, numeric representation, signing, and immutable provenance. This breadth is appropriate to the declared N07-B05 objective and is not a uniqueness defect. The identified blockers are the specific question-identity changes, the §4.3 longest-key cue, and i003’s unsupported name-reservation premise—not a demand for 18 unrelated concepts.

verifiedPrimarySources.title: Protocol Buffers proto3 Language Guide
verifiedPrimarySources.supports: Additive binary fields, unknown-field compatibility, defaults/presence, enum zero/default rules, reserving removed field identifiers.

verifiedPrimarySources.title: Protocol Buffers Field Presence Application Note
verifiedPrimarySources.supports: Explicit versus implicit proto3 field presence and zero-value distinction.

verifiedPrimarySources.title: ProtoJSON Format
verifiedPrimarySources.supports: JSON field names/json_name, int64 string representation, enum names/alias serialization, null semantics.

verifiedPrimarySources.title: Protocol Buffer Serialization Is Not Canonical
verifiedPrimarySources.supports: Ordinary/deterministic protobuf serialization is not canonical; unknown fields complicate generic fingerprints; application-specific canonical projection is recommended.

sourceReview.limitedReference: For i012/i015/i017, the source URL points to Martin Fowler’s Version Number catalog page. Direct open was unavailable in this review; the current hypotheticals make immutable-revision and history needs explicit, but that link was not independently confirmed to support those particular storage decisions. No claim is made that it proves a protobuf rule.

limitations: No full 144-question cross-unit comparison against accepted945 N01–N06 decisions is claimed; that remains the final N07 review.
